messages.author: 4391a11a04482aae
messages.subject: Detection function error
parts:
Hai Eric,

Am working on some follow-up distance sampling analysis were I have chopped (using R) my transects into 200m segments resulting in about 12000 rows across 4 regions of the study area. When I run the analysis using 500m segments, its running okay and producing results but once I segment the same data set into 200m segments, I get this error telling me there are no records in one of the regions which is not the case as I have checked the data and confirmed that there are records in all the regions, is there another issue I should be checking for?

 ##Estimating Detection Functions
>                            detfc.hr.null <- ds(distdata, max(distdata$distance), key="hr", adjustment=NULL)
Fitting hazard-rate key function
Warning in process.data(data, meta.data, check = FALSE) :
  no truncation distance specified; using largest observed distance
AIC= -1040.562
Error in create.varstructure(model, region.table, sample.table, obs.table,  : 
  Following regions have no samples -  N.Other

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Detection function error
parts:
Hai Eric,

I did manage to use the method of combining multiple detection functions - lots of progress although my population estimate is very high compared to the independent data sets (ebird records - just for validation and historic surveys on the species).
I wonder if the structure of my count data could be an issue? The species is clustered by nature thus I have set the group argument as TRUE in the dsm formula and of course Distance sampling in R is giving me estimates of both individuals and clusters with an average cluster size of 12. I wonder if the problem could be with the structure my field data; I have 194 records which are mostly 2s (as the mode) but there are 3 instances where i had extremely large clusters from drinking points encountered along transects with 109,153 and 215 birds and it seems these two very large counts are increasing the average and driving the estimate up. Is there another way to deal with this? I have tried to get multiple detection functions using transect type (walking or driving), transect design (random or track) and region (protected area versus open area) to see if any of these are possible sources of bias.
Am not sure whatelse to try, any pointers?

Chaona

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Detection function error
parts:
Chaona

You are outside my range of experience with this sort of analysis. I gather you are using your multiple detection functions to then build a spatial (dsm) model. It is possible that the transects where your aggregations occurred could cause your estimates to be very large (extrapolation of these densities to other places in the study area with the same set of spatial covariates).

To see if this is plausible, set groups=TRUE, so you produce spatial estimates of group density. Multiply these cell-specific group densities by 2 (which is your modal group size) and see what estimates you produce. I vaguely remember work in which authors built a spatial model of group density and coupled it with a spatial model of group size; but I can't bring citations to mind. That might be beyond what you want to undertake.

parts:
As I said, all this is speculative. Build the dsm model as you have, but with group=FALSE; giving a density surface for groups. Build (outside the distance sampling framework) another gam with the response being group size. This would produce cell-specific estimated group sizes, coupled with cell-specific group densities from the dsm. Combine the two manually, carrying uncertainty of both into your estimate of cell-specific individual density.  I've not done this, hence the speculative nature.

Subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Detection function error

Hai Eric,
 do you mean including the mode in my dsm formula?
I currently have it like this;
formula_covar1 <- count ~ s(X,Y) + s(Tree_cover) + s(Grassland) + s(Cropland) + s(Dist2water)
dsm.covar1 <- dsm(formula = formula_covar1,
                  engine = "gam",
                  group = TRUE,
                  ddf.obj = dd_list,
                  segment.data = segs,
                  observation.data = obs,
                  family = quasipoisson(link = "log"),
                  method = "REML")

Or do you mean to somehow get the groups argument into the distance sampling analysis? Since that's where the detection functions used in the dsm are generated?

Chaona

On Tue, May 30, 2023 at 1:51 PM Eric Rexstad <Eric.R...@st-andrews.ac.uk> wrote:
Chaona

You are outside my range of experience with this sort of analysis. I gather you are using your multiple detection functions to then build a spatial (dsm) model. It is possible that the transects where your aggregations occurred could cause your estimates to be very large (extrapolation of these densities to other places in the study area with the same set of spatial covariates).

To see if this is plausible, set groups=TRUE, so you produce spatial estimates of group density. Multiply these cell-specific group densities by 2 (which is your modal group size) and see what estimates you produce. I vaguely remember work in which authors built a spatial model of group density and coupled it with a spatial model of group size; but I can't bring citations to mind. That might be beyond what you want to undertake.

Subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Detection function error
 
Hai Eric,

I did manage to use the method of combining multiple detection functions - lots of progress although my population estimate is very high compared to the independent data sets (ebird records - just for validation and historic surveys on the species).
I wonder if the structure of my count data could be an issue? The species is clustered by nature thus I have set the group argument as TRUE in the dsm formula and of course Distance sampling in R is giving me estimates of both individuals and clusters with an average cluster size of 12. I wonder if the problem could be with the structure my field data; I have 194 records which are mostly 2s (as the mode) but there are 3 instances where i had extremely large clusters from drinking points encountered along transects with 109,153 and 215 birds and it seems these two very large counts are increasing the average and driving the estimate up. Is there another way to deal with this? I have tried to get multiple detection functions using transect type (walking or driving), transect design (random or track) and region (protected area versus open area) to see if any of these are possible sources of bias.
Am not sure whatelse to try, any pointers?

Chaona

Cheers

On Wed, Apr 19, 2023 at 11:00 AM Eric Rexstad <Eric.R...@st-andrews.ac.uk> wrote:
Chaona

Pleased to hear you sorted your create.varstructure​ problem.

There are recent developments with the dsm​ package for dealing with situations such as you describe. The manuscript title explains it well
Miller DL, Fifield D, Wakefield E, Sigourney DB. 2021. Extending density surface models to include multiple and double-observer survey data. PeerJ 9:e12113 https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.12113
I have had no experience conducting such an analysis, but there are supplemental materials associated with the manuscript that should give you a template to follow.

Subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Detection function error
 
Thanks Eric, indeed it was the Sample Labels columns causing problems - I deleted the whole column and added a new one, which seems to have sorted out the problem.

Away from that, do you have another recommendation on how to handle mixed transect (walking and driving) in distance sampling? I have data with both and am not sure if just having transect type as a covariate is enough to highlight the significance or if I should be doing something else. My DSM models from the best DS analysis are overfitting the species abundance estimates and giving Inf values.

Chaona

I would take the message at face value, examine what you have defined as the Sample.Label​ and examine a table(Sample.Label, Region.Label)` begin looking for problems.  I understand there are lots of rows to examine, but there's a problem in there somewhere.
